lens: Drawing appeal, contour and scale simplification
stage: Independent concept recommendation before partner discussion or image generation; not approval of unbuilt art.
independence: This initial position was saved before reading the partner's new recommendation.

recommendation.three: Do not start with three; it creates a second mini-cast across already occupied areas. Consider only if the two-cameo comparison demonstrates spare visual capacity.
recommendation.fullCast: Reject for this composition: the reference works as a group portrait, while this park already has three deliberate moth appearances and a dominant foreground working scene.
recommendation.why: Two can be a subordinate discovery about the tools/companions around Nag. More bright logo faces risk turning a personal portrait into an AI-brand ensemble. The existing coder, builder and resting moth already carry the narrative.
recommendation.placement: One compact pair in the middle/background flower-and-shrub band just behind the rear-left worktable post. Both watch the builder quietly. Keep clear air around the builder's head/hammer and the resting moth, and leave the winding path open. No second cluster near the tree in the first audition.
recommendation.scale: Each entire cameo, including limbs, approximately one-third to two-fifths of the middle builder moth's full height and distinctly below the resting moth's scale. Use depth, partial foliage occlusion and shared warm lighting; do not enlarge them merely to preserve a logo at phone size.
recommendation.material: Adapt bodies to the same painted park lighting and subdued middle-distance edge contrast. Avoid the reference's cluster of bright white/red/blue tiles, blanket, basket and extra props. Specific logo identities remain owner-selected and should not be guessed from uncertain forms.
recommendation.hardForegroundConstraint: Absolutely no companion near, on, beside or in front of the bench; none in the foreground or on its props. The foreground work area remains exclusively the original moth, bench and requested MacBook. Do not sneak a logo face into a mug, laptop screen, foreground leaf or bench decoration.

failureCriteria: Remove the cameos if either is a competing first-read focal point with the foreground face/MacBook or if the worktable becomes visually about the logo pair rather than Nag building.
Remove or reposition if cameo limbs/marks merge with the moth's antennae, wings, hammer or resting silhouette, or if they plug the central path that links the existing scenes.

If recognizability at the actual narrow banner requires bigger, sharper or brighter companions, accept their disappearance as tiny optional details or return to zero; do not violate the foreground constraint.
Reject any generated version that adds extra companions, a logo strip, textual labels, foreground symbols, or changes the moth's innocent anatomy.
verificationBeforeAnyAdoption: Compare current zero against the two-cameo render at original panoramic size and actual GitHub banner widths, including 846px desktop and 238px narrow use. Judge first-read hierarchy and silhouette separation, not the number of recognizable product marks. The tiny phone version may legitimately lose the cameo identities.

skills.practicalUse: Named-axis zero-versus-two comparison, restrained secondary detail, actual application scale, preserve authored silhouette and foreground hierarchy. The explicit current owner constraint supersedes earlier possible cameo placement.
skills.exceptions: No mandatory commercial-site imagery, hover motion or full prototype picker is needed for a static concept. No numerical score or approval is assigned before rendering. No image generation, browser operation or source edit was performed.

limits: No proposed cameo variant exists yet, so overload at final size is a hypothesis.
Reference product identities were not verified and are not inferred.
No unfamiliar-human recognition, attachment or association outcomes have been measured.
The park image was displayed at 2048x683 from a 2172x724 source; this is not a physical-phone preview.

pairDiscussion.partnerEvidence: Direct message after both independent files were saved; A recommends two as a quiet group left of/behind workshop, around one-third builder height, keeping tree and foreground unchanged.
pairDiscussion.agreement: Both independently prefer a bounded two-cameo audition against the zero-cameo control. One group watches box-making from behind the rear-left workshop area. Start at approximately one-third of the builder's full height, with shared painterly lighting and no extra blanket/basket/logo props.
pairDiscussion.challengeAndResolution: B distinguishes distracting bright specks from simply losing product identity at 238px. Cameos may become inconspicuous optional detail; never enlarge or brighten them merely to make logos identifiable on a narrow banner. B's independent upper scale bound of two-fifths is not the initial test target.
pairDiscussion.acceptedRecommendation: Test two small supporting companions as one quiet middle/background group behind the left workshop area, about one-third builder height, watching the building moth. Keep the resting scene unchanged and keep all companions out of the foreground and away from/on neither bench nor its props. Compare with the moth-only control before any adoption.
pairDiscussion.scope: Concept-test recommendation only; no numeric score, generation, publication or approval of an unbuilt result.
pairDiscussion.partnerExplicitConfirmation: Visual A directly confirmed the same joint recommendation and phone-scale nuance; no substantive difference remains.
